brief: Mechtild of Magdeburg was born in 1210 and in 1233 joined a group of Beguines, women devoted to charitable work, living in community under temporary vows. She had powerful religious experiences, dominated by the thought of “all things in God and God in all things”. She wrote these down in a book called The Flowing Light of the Godhead. She was also a trenchant critic of abuses in the church of the day. This led to some strong opposition. She spent her last years in a convent in Saxony and died there in 1297.
